# Introduction

Alpha- and beta-thalassaemia genotypes are chromosome-haplotype states, not merely
lists of independent VCF records. At the HBA locus, clinically relevant states can
differ in copy number, copy order, hybrid sequence, recombination junction and
linked small variants. At the HBB locus, promoter, splice, coding and structural
variants can occur in cis or trans and their phenotypic effect depends on the
primary beta-globin genotype and co-inherited modifiers.

## Initial thesis scope

The original project was a retrospective analysis of thalassaemia genetic testing
at Dubai Genetics Center with five linked aims:

1. characterize the reported HBA and HBB landscape in a diverse referral cohort;
2. investigate whether co-inherited HBA states modify haematological parameters in
   HBB carriers;
3. assess representation of cohort variants in public genomic databases;
4. characterize a separate group evaluated using ONT long-read sequencing; and
5. compare the reported diagnostic spectra of conventional Sanger/gap-PCR and ONT
   testing eras.

The two clinical tables are not a paired re-testing cohort, and both contain
selectively reported clinically relevant findings. Aim 5 is therefore an
ascertainment-aware comparison of report distributions, not a direct platform
sensitivity study.

## Computational contribution

NanoGlobin connects the cohort study to an executable assay model. The cohort
identifies locally relevant alleles, compound states and nomenclature failures.
The software asks whether a declared primer design can physically generate
products that distinguish those states, then scores observed ONT molecules against
the resulting chromosome-haplotype candidates.
